text:
[LSER.8.6.5] **A fact's sample is absorbed exactly once, for the life of that
fact.** Absorption is tracked per fact, not per pump and not per key, and three
cases follow that the pump-scoped rule above makes non-obvious:

- A **no-op reassertion** produces no second sample. The adapter returns the
  existing fact and the fact has already been absorbed ([LSER.8.5.1]).
- A **retract** ends the fact, and with it the record that it was absorbed. A
  later fact on the same key is a new fact and absorbs its own sample.
- A fact **superseded within a pump** still contributes. The absorption step
  runs after the agenda drains and by then the superseded fact is gone, so its
  sample must be resolved when it is superseded and held until the step runs —
  otherwise N asserts against one key before a pump would contribute one sample
  instead of N, against [LSER.8.5.1]'s "on every meaningful fact update".

The third is the one a second implementation gets wrong, because it is invisible
until a program updates the same key twice between pumps.
